linux.label: Linux
linux.notes: Linux packaging and live-host verification are deferred; the portable runtime remains testable but is outside this release.

macos.label: macOS
macos.notes: The relocatable plugin runtime is gated on a native macOS runner before release.

windows.label: Windows
windows.notes: The relocatable plugin runtime is gated on a native Windows runner before release.

profiles.name: Generic Agent Plugin
profiles.summary: Portable Agent Plugins v1 floor: Agent Skills plus MCP, without host lifecycle guarantees.

capabilities.notes: A client may expose a vault directory; the plugin format does not own it.
The v1 package format defines stdio and Streamable HTTP configuration.
Skills are discovered from the fixed skills/ directory.
Hooks are outside the Agent Plugins v1 core contract.
Session events are client-specific.
Scheduling is client-owned, not portable plugin behavior.
Prompt UX is defined by the host client.
This descriptor describes the v1 package contract itself.

limitations: The package format does not define hooks, commands, agents, UI, permissions, or updates.

profiles.name: BB
profiles.summary: Native BB plugin for read-only Dex status, capability inspection, and work briefing.

capabilities.notes: The plugin reads the user-selected local Dex vault with containment checks.
The native BB integration uses BB tools and RPC rather than MCP.
Dex skills are bundled in the BB plugin package.
The first BB release does not register lifecycle hooks.
Dex status and briefing are available through native BB panels and tools, not automatic session injection.
The first BB release does not schedule jobs.
BB exposes native tools, CLI commands, and a Dex panel.
A standalone bb-plugin-dex package is built and SDK-verified; live BB installation remains unreleased.

limitations: The package is read-only and unreleased; live bb CLI installation has not yet been verified.
The standalone package currently targets macOS. BB's documented Windows route uses WSL2, which remains in Dex's deferred Linux lane.

profiles.name: ChatGPT Work companion
profiles.summary: ChatGPT Work desktop can load the same local plugin package after a person installs it from a local marketplace and grants a Dex vault folder. That desktop journey is not proven yet. ChatGPT web needs a separately hosted HTTPS door.

capabilities.notes: Desktop can use a local vault only after the person grants that folder in Work locally; web cannot reach it.
Local stdio works on desktop after the plugin is installed; web requires a separately hosted HTTPS MCP service.
Skills are bundled in the shared desktop plugin package.
Bundled hooks require local host support and user trust.
SessionStart context is available only where local plugin hooks run.
The portable plugin does not promise a scheduler.
Conversation prompts are host-native.
The plugin uses the shared desktop plugin format. A person installs it from a local marketplace in ChatGPT desktop; this is not a recorded live journey.

limitations: A person still has to open ChatGPT Work on a real desktop, install the local Dex plugin from a local marketplace, and grant the Dex vault folder. Detection tests and CI do not prove that journey.
ChatGPT web needs a public HTTPS MCP service; the local-vault remote bridge is not implemented in this release.
A shared plugin cache on disk is not proof someone opened ChatGPT Work.

profiles.name: Claude Code
profiles.summary: Dex's Tier 3 reference harness with native skills, MCP, hooks, and session lifecycle support.

capabilities.notes: Local filesystem access is available in the active project.
The package includes Claude's native .mcp.json configuration.
The portable skill catalogue is bundled in the plugin.
PreToolUse safety and SessionStart context hooks are bundled and reviewed at install.
SessionStart context runs automatically after the plugin is trusted.
Dex's OS-scheduled jobs remain independent of the chat harness.
AskUserQuestion is available when the client provides it.
The same package includes a native Claude plugin manifest.

limitations: Host-specific features beyond the shared SessionStart and PreToolUse hooks remain Claude-only.

profiles.name: Claude Desktop
profiles.summary: One-click MCP Bundle for Dex's local read-only tools in Claude Desktop on macOS and Windows.

capabilities.notes: The user selects a local Dex vault when installing the desktop extension.
A validated .mcpb artifact exposes Dex's read-only MCP tools locally.
Claude plugins carry Dex skills; the MCPB artifact itself carries tools rather than skills.
Claude Desktop chat does not run plugin hooks; hooks remain available in Claude Code and Cowork.
The MCP Bundle is a tool surface, not a session lifecycle host.
Dex background jobs are installed by the operating-system adapter, independently of Claude Desktop.
Desktop conversation prompts are host-native.
Claude Desktop local tools use MCPB rather than the Agent Plugins package format.

limitations: The desktop bundle requires Dex's supported Python runtime and exposes read-only MCP tools; Claude Desktop chat does not run Dex hooks.

profiles.name: Codex
profiles.summary: Native Dex plugin for Codex CLI and desktop with skills, read-only MCP tools, and shared lifecycle hooks.

capabilities.notes: The active workspace is available to the agent.
The package includes a native Codex MCP configuration.
The generated skills and release-time AGENTS.md bootstrap are portable.
Bundled hooks require explicit user trust before Codex runs them.
SessionStart context runs automatically after the plugin is trusted.
The portable plugin does not assume a Codex scheduler.
Conversation input is host-native.
The package includes a native .codex-plugin manifest.

limitations: Codex IDE extensions do not currently load plugins; use Codex CLI or desktop for this package.

profiles.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
profiles.summary: Open Plugin Spec package for Copilot CLI with skills, MCP, and the family PreToolUse refusal file. A person still has to install the reviewed local plugin and start the CLI from the Dex folder.

capabilities.notes: The current working directory is the vault after the person starts the CLI from the Dex folder.
The Open Plugin Spec package includes a relocatable stdio MCP server in mcp.json.
Copilot CLI loads skills from the installed plugin.
The shipped package includes the family PreToolUse refusal hook file. A person still has to install the local plugin. Fixture-proved; not a recorded live walk.
Available lifecycle events depend on the installed Copilot CLI version.
No Dex scheduler contract is assumed.
CLI interaction is host-native.
A person installs the reviewed local Open Plugin Spec package with copilot plugin install. This is not a recorded live journey.

limitations: A person still has to install the reviewed local plugin with `copilot plugin install ./packages/dex-agent-plugin` and start the CLI from the Dex folder. Detection tests and CI do not prove that journey.
Ubuntu Cloud is not a person opening this terminal. No recorded live session exists.
The family PreToolUse refusal hook is fixture-proved in this package. That is not a live walk.

profiles.name: Claude Cowork
profiles.summary: Native Claude plugin for Cowork skills, hooks, and folder work, with a public-endpoint requirement for external connectors.

capabilities.notes: Folder access depends on explicit desktop permission granted by the user.
Cowork external connectors require a public internet endpoint; the bundled local stdio server is not claimed.
The native Claude plugin carries Dex's portable skills.
Cowork plugins can run the bundled hooks after installation and trust review.
Hook availability depends on the Cowork task surface and granted folder access.
Cowork can schedule host tasks, but Dex does not yet install schedule templates.
Desktop conversation prompts are host-native.
The same package includes a native Claude plugin manifest.

limitations: The local stdio MCP bridge is not exposed as a Cowork external connector; that needs a separately secured public endpoint.

profiles.name: Cursor
profiles.summary: Native Cursor plugin plus the open Agent Plugins package, with shared skills, MCP, context, and safety hooks.

capabilities.notes: The open workspace is available to Cursor Agent.
Cursor loads the same relocatable MCP server from the plugin package.
Cursor supports Agent Skills and the Agent Plugins open standard.
Native sessionStart and preToolUse hooks map to Dex's shared context and safety core after workspace trust.
Local Cursor sessions inject context automatically; cloud agents intentionally do not run sessionStart.
The plugin does not assume Cursor Automations; Dex uses its operating-system scheduler.
Agent chat interaction is host-native.
Cursor loads Agent Plugins directly and also accepts the included native Cursor manifest.

limitations: Cursor cloud agents do not run sessionStart; local safety hooks require workspace trust.

profiles.name: Gemini CLI
profiles.summary: Native Gemini CLI extension generated from Dex's shared skills, MCP, context, and safety core.

capabilities.notes: The current Gemini workspace is available to the extension.
The extension declares Dex's relocatable stdio MCP server with extensionPath variables.
Gemini CLI extensions discover Agent Skills from skills/.
SessionStart and BeforeTool map to the shared Dex context and safety core after trust review.
SessionStart injects current Dex context on startup, resume, and clear.
The extension does not assume a Gemini scheduler; Dex uses its operating-system scheduler.
CLI interaction is host-native.
Gemini uses its native extension format; the artifact is generated from the same canonical package sources.

limitations: Gemini uses a separately built extension artifact because its fixed hooks file has a different schema from Claude's.

profiles.name: Kiro
profiles.summary: Kiro can load the same local Agent Plugins package as a custom power. It wakes Dex when you name it. A person still has to import the reviewed folder. Family plugin hooks are not claimed.

capabilities.notes: The open Dex folder is the vault after the person starts Kiro there.
Kiro loads mcp.json from the imported power and manages those servers with the power.
Skills come from the shipped package skills/ folder.
Kiro's first-party hooks are workspace files under .kiro/hooks with a different schema. Powers do not load the family plugin hook file. Safety stays an explicit MCP check.
The power loads when the person names Dex or another listed keyword.
No Dex scheduler contract is assumed.
Kiro chat is host-native.
A person imports packages/dex-agent-plugin as a custom power. This is not a recorded live journey.

limitations: A person still has to import ./packages/dex-agent-plugin from the Kiro Powers panel and name Dex so the power wakes. Detection tests and CI do not prove that journey.
If auto-detect is empty or names VS Code or Cursor, confirm Kiro in /setup.
Ubuntu Cloud is not a person opening Kiro. No recorded live session exists.
Hooks are not included in this path; shared safety remains an explicit MCP check.

profiles.name: Pi
profiles.summary: Local coding agent with workspace files, Agent Skills, and lifecycle events, but no built-in Dex MCP or scheduler promise.

capabilities.notes: The workspace is available to Pi extensions and skills.
Pi has no built-in MCP client; its native Dex extension supplies direct tools instead.
AGENTS.md and Agent Skills are the portable instruction surface.
The native Dex extension maps Pi events rather than pretending they are Claude hooks.
The Dex Pi extension observes native session lifecycle events.
No Dex scheduler is assumed.
Pi exposes interactive conversation input.
Pi uses its native Dex extension rather than an Agent Plugins loader.

limitations: MCP is intentionally not claimed; use the native Dex Pi extension for tools and lifecycle integration.

profiles.name: Visual Studio Code
profiles.summary: VS Code can load the same local Agent Plugins package after a person turns on plugin settings that stay off by default. The family PreToolUse refusal file is included.

capabilities.notes: The open Dex folder is the vault after the person starts VS Code there.
VS Code reads mcp.json from the local plugin after the plugin is enabled.
Skills come from the shipped package skills/ folder.
The shipped package includes the family PreToolUse refusal hook file. Plugin settings stay off until a person turns them on. Fixture-proved; not a recorded live walk.
Plugin load depends on the person turning on chat.plugins.enabled and pointing chat.pluginLocations at the shipped package.
No Dex scheduler contract is assumed.
VS Code chat is host-native.
A person enables chat.plugins.enabled and registers ./packages/dex-agent-plugin in chat.pluginLocations. This is not a recorded live journey.

limitations: VS Code plugin settings stay off by default. A person still has to turn on chat.plugins.enabled, point chat.pluginLocations at ./packages/dex-agent-plugin, and reload. Detection tests and CI do not prove that journey.
If auto-detect is empty or names Cursor or Kiro, confirm VS Code in /setup.
Ubuntu Cloud is not a person opening VS Code. No recorded live session exists.
The family PreToolUse refusal hook is fixture-proved in this package. That is not a live walk.
